할아버지.x: My grandfather lives in the countryside.
할아버지.t: Pronounced [하라버지]. Also a polite way to address any elderly man.

감기.x: I've had a cold since yesterday, so my throat hurts.
감기.t: Use 감기에 걸리다 'to catch a cold' — note the particle 에.

카드.t: Use 로: 카드로 계산하다 / 카드로 내다 = pay by card.

서다.ex: 버스 정류장 앞에 사람들이 서 있어요.
서다.x: People are standing in front of the bus stop.
서다.e: 일어서다 = to stand up. For buses and cars it means 'to stop'.
서다.t: Use 서 있다 for the state 'be standing'.

켜다.m: to turn on, to switch on (lights, devices)
켜다.x: The room is dark. Please turn on the light.
켜다.e: Opposite: 끄다 (turn off). 불을 켜다 = turn on the light.

개다.x: In the afternoon, the rain will stop and the skies will clear.
개다.e: Homonym warning: 개다 also means 'to fold' clothes, and 개 alone is 'dog'.
개다.t: You'll mostly hear 개다 in forecasts; in conversation people often say 날씨가 맑아졌어요.

개다.x: I folded the dry laundry and put it in the closet.
개다.e: Homonym warning: 개다 also means 'to clear up' (weather), and 개 alone is 'dog'.
개다.t: Use 개다 for clothes and bedding (이불을 개다); for paper, use 접다.

만화.ex: 저는 주말에 만화를 보는 것을 좋아해요.
만화.x: I like reading comics on the weekend.
만화.e: Literally 'casual pictures'; English 'manhwa' means Korean comics, like 'manga' for Japanese.

떨어지다.m: to fall, to drop; to fail (an exam)
떨어지다.x: I studied hard, but I failed the exam.
떨어지다.e: Basic meaning is 'to fall'; failing an exam is falling off the list.
떨어지다.t: Also used for prices or grades going down: 성적이 떨어졌어요.

현재.x: The current temperature in Seoul is 5 degrees below zero.
현재.e: Literally 'appearing and existing' — what is here now.
현재.t: 현재 is more formal than 지금 and is common in news and reports.

하하.ex: 그 얘기를 듣고 다들 하하 웃었어요.
하하.x: Everyone laughed 'ha-ha' when they heard that story.
하하.e: 의성어 (sound word) for open, hearty laughter. Its dark-vowel partner 허허 is a deeper, calmer laugh, typical of older men.
하하.t: In text messages, ㅎㅎ is a soft, friendly laugh, while ㅋㅋ is closer to 'lol'.

시설.ex: 이 아파트는 운동 시설이 잘 되어 있어요.
시설.x: This apartment complex has good fitness facilities.

보호하다.x: Sunscreen protects your skin from sunlight.
보호하다.t: Pattern: A로부터 B를 보호하다 = protect B from A.

인간관계.x: In work life, relationships with people are really important.

불안.ex: 미래에 대한 불안 때문에 잠을 못 자요.
불안.x: I can't sleep because of anxiety about the future.
불안.t: Pronounced [부란]: the ㄹ carries over to the next syllable.

본인.m: the person in question, oneself; (formal) you
본인.ex: 신청은 반드시 본인이 직접 하셔야 합니다.

그러므로.ex: 운동은 건강에 좋습니다. 그러므로 매일 운동해야 합니다.
그러므로.x: Exercise is good for your health. Therefore, you should exercise every day.
그러므로.e: 그러하다 'to be so' + -므로 'because': because it is so.
그러므로.t: Mostly used in writing, speeches, and essays; in conversation, 그래서 sounds natural.

없애다.m: to get rid of, to remove, to eliminate
없애다.x: I want to get rid of the bad smell in the room.
없애다.e: Built from 없다 'to not exist' plus a causative ending: literally 'make it not exist'.

인출하다.x: I withdrew cash at the bank.
인출하다.t: 현금 인출기 means 'ATM'; the opposite action is 입금하다 'to deposit'.

지도하다.m: to guide, to coach, to supervise, to instruct
지도하다.x: Mr. Park coaches our soccer team.
지도하다.t: Don't confuse with 지도 'map': same sound, different word.

고려하다.ex: 가격과 위치를 고려해서 이 집을 골랐어요.
고려하다.x: I chose this house taking price and location into account.

활기차다.ex: 아침 일찍 가 보면 시장은 언제나 활기차요.
활기차다.x: If you go early in the morning, the market is always lively.
활기차다.e: 활기 'lively energy' + native 차다 'to be full': full of life.

자산.x: That company has over one trillion won in assets.

주목을 받다.forms: 주목을 받다 · 받아요 · 받았어요 · 받을 거예요
주목을 받다.m: to attract attention, to be in the spotlight
주목을 받다.ex: 그 영화는 해외에서도 큰 주목을 받았어요.
주목을 받다.x: The movie got a lot of attention overseas too.
주목을 받다.e: 주목 is literally 'pouring your eyes' onto something.

첨단.m: cutting edge, state of the art, high tech
첨단.e: Literally 'pointed tip' — the very front of progress.
첨단.t: Usually used before a noun: 첨단 기술, 첨단 산업, 첨단 장비.

약삭빠르다.m: shrewd, calculating, quick to look out for oneself
약삭빠르다.x: He shrewdly looked out only for his own interests.
약삭빠르다.e: Ends in 빠르다 'fast' — quick to grab an advantage.

왠지.forms: 왠지 + feeling: 왠지 기분이 좋아요, 왠지 불안해요
왠지.ex: 오늘은 왠지 좋은 일이 생길 것 같아요.
왠지.x: Somehow I feel like something good will happen today.
왠지.e: Contraction of 왜인지 'why it is (I don't know)'.
왠지.t: Classic spelling trap: 왠지 (from 왜) vs. 웬 'what kind of', as in 웬일이에요?

급격히.ex: 최근 몇 년 사이에 출생률이 급격히 떨어졌습니다.
급격히.x: The birth rate has dropped sharply in recent years.
급격히.t: Pronounced [급껴키]; a TOPIK graph-writing favorite: 급격히 증가하다/감소하다.

되찾다.m: to get back, to regain, to recover
되찾다.x: I got my lost wallet back at the police station.
되찾다.e: 되- 'back' + 찾다 'to find': finding what you once had.
되찾다.t: Common with abstract nouns: 건강을 되찾다, 웃음을 되찾다, 자신감을 되찾다.

뛰어넘다.m: to jump over, to leap over; to overcome, to surpass; to skip
뛰어넘다.x: The cat leapt lightly over the wall.

한숨을 쉬다.forms: 한숨을 쉬어요 · 한숨을 쉬었어요 · 깊은 한숨을 쉬다
한숨을 쉬다.ex: 시험 결과를 보고 그는 깊은 한숨을 쉬었어요.
한숨을 쉬다.x: He let out a deep sigh after seeing his test results.
한숨을 쉬다.t: 한숨(을) 돌리다 is different: it signals relief, 'to catch one's breath.'

기원.ex: 이 음식의 기원은 조선 시대로 알려져 있어요.
기원.x: This dish is known to date back to the Joseon era.
기원.t: A homonym 기원 means 'prayer, wish', as in 평화를 기원합니다.

범주.ex: 이 문제는 개인의 범주를 넘어선 사회 문제예요.
범주.x: This is a social issue that goes beyond the individual.
범주.e: Literally 'pattern and class': a box that ideas are sorted into.

유대.ex: 운동은 가족 간의 유대를 강화하는 데 좋아요.
유대.x: Exercising together is good for strengthening family bonds.
유대.e: Literally 'string and belt': what ties people together.
유대.t: Homonym: 유대 also means 'Judea, Jewish', as in 유대인.

의의.ex: 이번 회의는 두 나라가 처음 만났다는 데 의의가 있어요.
의의.x: This meeting is significant in that the two countries met for the first time.
의의.t: Pronounced [의이]; X다는 데 의의가 있다 = 'it is meaningful in that X'.

꾸벅꾸벅.ex: 점심을 먹고 수업 시간에 꾸벅꾸벅 졸았어요.
꾸벅꾸벅.x: After lunch, I kept nodding off in class.
꾸벅꾸벅.e: 의태어 (manner word) for the head dropping forward and coming back up, as when dozing off or bowing.
꾸벅꾸벅.t: Single 꾸벅 is one quick bow: 꾸벅 인사했어요.

감찰.ex: 검찰은 소속 직원들에 대한 감찰을 시작했습니다.
감찰.x: The prosecution began an internal investigation of its staff.

관할.x: This area is not under the jurisdiction of Seoul City.

원조.ex: 한국은 과거에 원조를 받았지만 지금은 원조를 주는 나라입니다.
원조.x: Korea once received aid, but now it is a country that gives aid.
원조.t: 원조 on a restaurant sign (원조 할매집) means 'the original', a different word.

주도.x: This event was prepared under the students' leadership.

은유.x: 'My heart is a lake' is a classic example of a metaphor.

신설하다.m: to newly establish, to create (a department, route)
신설하다.x: The school will create a new AI department next year.

여겨지다.m: to be regarded, to be considered, to be seen as
여겨지다.ex: 이 작품은 그의 최고 걸작으로 여겨집니다.
여겨지다.x: This work is regarded as his greatest masterpiece.
여겨지다.e: Passive of 여기다 'to regard, to consider' with -어지다.
여겨지다.t: Pattern A로 여겨지다 = to be seen as A; very common in formal writing.

점잖다.x: He speaks in a dignified way and acts carefully too.
점잖다.e: Probably from 젊지 않다 'not young' — mature, hence dignified.
점잖다.t: Pronounced [점잔타]; 점잖은 is [점자는] — the ㅎ is silent before a vowel.

다소.x: Tomorrow will be somewhat colder than today.
다소.t: Formal, common in news and weather reports; in casual speech use 좀 or 약간.

갈팡질팡.m: this way and that, in confusion; wavering
갈팡질팡.x: When I first came to Seoul, I wandered around confused in the subway station.
갈팡질팡.e: Rhyming pair; picture someone darting this way and that, getting nowhere.
갈팡질팡.t: Also for indecision: 갈팡질팡하다 'to waver, be unable to decide'.

재무.ex: 그는 회사에서 재무 업무를 담당하고 있어요.
재무.x: He's in charge of finance at his company.
재무.t: 재무 is for a company's money matters; 재정 is more for government or household finances.

동정심.ex: 길에서 떨고 있는 강아지를 보니 동정심이 생겼어요.
동정심.x: Seeing the puppy shivering on the street, I felt sympathy for it.
동정심.e: Literally 'heart that shares the same feeling'.

이산화 탄소.ex: 자동차는 많은 양의 이산화 탄소를 배출합니다.
이산화 탄소.x: Cars emit a large amount of carbon dioxide.
이산화 탄소.e: Literally 'two-oxygen carbon': 산 here stands for oxygen (산소).
이산화 탄소.t: It is very often written without a space: 이산화탄소.

천대하다.m: to treat with contempt, to treat as inferior
천대하다.x: In the old days, there was a culture of looking down on merchants.

인싸.ex: 우리 반 인싸는 친구가 정말 많아요.
인싸.x: The most popular kid in our class has tons of friends.
인싸.t: Casual slang. The opposite is 아싸 (from 'outsider'); 인싸템 = a trendy must-have item.

프사.ex: 프사 바꿨네요? 사진 진짜 잘 나왔어요.
프사.x: You changed your profile pic? It came out really well.
프사.t: Casual. Change it is 프사를 바꾸다; friends often notice and comment.

스트리머.ex: 그 스트리머는 매일 밤 게임 방송을 해요.
스트리머.x: That streamer does a gaming stream every night.
스트리머.t: Streamers are also called 인터넷 방송인 or BJ (Konglish 'broadcasting jockey'). Go live: 방송을 켜다; end the stream: 방송을 끄다.

소추.ex: 국회는 대통령에 대한 탄핵 소추안을 통과시켰습니다.
소추.x: The National Assembly passed the motion to impeach the president.
소추.e: Literally 'sue and pursue'; mostly seen in 탄핵소추 'impeachment'.

군자.m: a man of virtue, a noble person (Confucian ideal)
군자.ex: 군자는 어려울 때에도 예의를 지킨다고 해요.
군자.x: It is said that a person of virtue keeps their manners even in hard times.
군자.e: Literally 'a lord's son' — later, anyone noble in character.
군자.t: Common in sayings like 군자는 말이 적다; the opposite is 소인 or 소인배.

사양산업.ex: 한때 잘나가던 필름 산업은 이제 사양산업이 되었어요.
사양산업.x: The once-booming film industry has now become a declining industry.
사양산업.e: Literally 'setting-sun industry' — just like English 'sunset industry.'

극작가.ex: 그 극작가의 새 작품이 다음 주에 초연됩니다.
극작가.x: That playwright's new work premieres next week.
극작가.t: Pronounced [극짝까]: consonants after ㄱ become tense.

장독대.m: platform for sauce jars (where crocks of soy sauce, gochujang, etc. are kept)
장독대.ex: 할머니 집 장독대에는 된장 항아리가 가득했어요.
장독대.x: The jar platform at Grandma's house was full of doenjang crocks.
장독대.t: Pronounced [장똑때] — both 독 and 대 are tensed.

호연지기.m: a vast, free spirit; broad-minded vigor
호연지기.ex: 산에 올라 호연지기를 기르는 것도 좋아요.
호연지기.x: Climbing mountains is also a good way to nurture a broad, free spirit.
호연지기.e: From Mencius: a vast, upright energy that fills heaven and earth.
호연지기.t: Set phrase: 호연지기를 기르다 'to cultivate a great spirit'.

지탄하다.e: Literally 'flick with the finger' — pointing at someone in blame.
지탄하다.t: Most often passive in meaning: 사회적 지탄을 받다 'to face public condemnation'.

타진하다.m: to sound out, to feel out; to percuss (medical)
타진하다.ex: 그 회사는 해외 진출 가능성을 타진하고 있어요.
타진하다.x: The company is sounding out the possibility of expanding overseas.
타진하다.e: Literally 'tap and examine' — like a doctor tapping a patient's chest.

걸출하다.ex: 그는 한국 문학사에서 가장 걸출한 시인 중 한 명이에요.
걸출하다.x: He is one of the most outstanding poets in Korean literary history.
걸출하다.e: Literally 'a hero who stands out' from the crowd.

공영방송.x: Public broadcasters must protect their fairness and independence.
공영방송.e: Literally 'publicly run broadcasting', funded mainly by license fees, like KBS.

변별하다.m: to discriminate, to distinguish, to tell apart
변별하다.ex: 아기는 생후 몇 달 만에 엄마 목소리를 변별할 수 있어요.
변별하다.x: A baby can tell its mother's voice apart within a few months of birth.
변별하다.t: 변별력 is common in test talk: a test 'with good 변별력' separates strong and weak students.

점화하다.m: to ignite, to light; to spark off (a controversy)
점화하다.ex: 개막식에서 성화를 점화하는 순간 관중이 환호했습니다.
점화하다.x: The crowd cheered the moment the Olympic torch was lit at the opening ceremony.
점화하다.e: Literally 'light a fire' — from cauldrons to debates.

가없다.x: I'm always grateful for my parents' boundless love.

혈혈단신.m: all alone in the world, without any family
혈혈단신.ex: 그는 혈혈단신으로 고향을 떠나 서울에 왔어요.
혈혈단신.x: He left his hometown and came to Seoul all on his own.
혈혈단신.t: Usually appears as 혈혈단신으로 'all alone, with no one to rely on.'

면역억제제.ex: 장기 이식 환자는 면역억제제를 꾸준히 먹어야 합니다.
면역억제제.x: Organ transplant patients must take immunosuppressants regularly.
면역억제제.e: Literally 'immunity + hold-down + drug'. Final -제 = medicine: 진통제, 소화제.
면역억제제.t: Pronounced [며녀걱쩨제]: sounds link across syllables and the ㅈ after ㄱ turns tense.
